newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says race row has not hurt Australia ties.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says race row has not hurt Australia ties.

text.p: Malaysia's ties with Canberra have not been damaged by anti-Asian remarks made by certain Australian politicians, Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday.
"Just because one or two MPs make very irresponsible statements, it should not affect relations," Anwar said.
"We are concerned over the ensuing debate, but I don't think this is reflective of the Australian government's position," said Anwar.
He was speaking to reporters after opening the 13th General Meeting and Seminar of the Asian Bankers' Association.
Anwar was also reacting to a call by a Malaysian political youth group to sever business and tourism ties with Australia following remarks by Australian member of parliament (MP) Pauline Hanson.
On September 10, the independent MP claimed that Australia was being swamped by Asians and called for a halt to immigration.
Her remarks sparked off debate inside and outside Australia.
"The Australian government is unequivocally committed to maintaining a non-discriminatory immigration policy," the Australian High Commission in Kuala Lumpur said in statement on Monday.
